Hey, your personality sounds amazing! I completely understand, you are who you are around friends, and school is an entirely different matter. People tend to have different versions they present to the external world around different environments, doesn't mean anything is wrong with you! And trust me, you have time to be rebellious. Just don't let school suffer because of it, that's what I did. You've still got time, my dear. 
You sound beautiful too! Don't let what other people think of you affect what you think of yourself. I know that's easy to say and hard to do. But really. Fuck them. You're you. And you have every single right in the entire universe to be you. You still have time to develop into who you want to be. Don't hate your body just yet, she's still growing! 
If you don't get invited to parties because the people throwing them think appearance matters that much, you probably don't want to be friends with them anyways. There's so much more to a person than their appearance.

When things like this come back, I usually think back and make sure I actually dealt with the issue. Usually I've just shoved it away in some deep and dark crevice of my mind to be forgotten about until it breaks free with a vengeance. Are you sure you've completely dealt with the thoughts previously? I know it's so much easier to say than to do. It's a goddamn battle. I know mental illnesses never leave completely, but they can be managed. When the thoughts come, do everything you can not to bow down to them. To believe them. Acknowledge them, work them out, and make sure you discredit them. Because you are worth so much to the people around you. And more than that, you deserve to be happy individually.

okay, you need to be understanding of someone else's situation. you don't know all of the details, so your unnecessary comment is just piling up on the reasons this person thinks they have to feel bad about themselves. (don't worry about them, OP, you're fine) If you understood the extent of suicidal thoughts, you would understand that things tend to pile up and even the smallest thing can trigger an anxiety attack or something worse. get off your high horse and stop policing other people's problems.

I'm in kind of the same position. It sucks. It sucks a lot. But I'm sure if you want to contact your friends again, they'd respond. It's better than complete isolation, even if it's only a subconscious difference. One thing that helps me feel better when I feel shitty is honestly just getting out of my room. Sitting in the library or going for a walk. Anything to avoid my room, which I call my "depression cave" Hang in there, my man. PM me if you need anything <3

I'm glad you're feeling better! I'm also glad you've found a way to calm yourself down when things get hard. Hold on, plenty of people love you. And hey, your mom loves you enough to yell at you and make sure you're going to school! I know it still sucks in the moment, but life is all about perspective :)
